analysis.support_psnr_note: pair0 re-measured in R2 at 40.68 dB (R1: 40.69/40.67); pair1/pair2 carried from R1 k-pair validation (pipeline unchanged; deterministic re-runs stable within 0.02 dB)
analysis.rationale: R2 re-ran run_full_analysis on pair0: signal report identical to R1 except residual_intensity_corr 0.5787->0.5739 (numerical noise), so the R1 interpretation stands (glass blur; stretch global; no third step). The only un-revisited axis was severity: R0/R1 bracketed both severities only with saturate_weaken_HSV:3 present. Under the corrected 2-step pipeline the contrast axis is a sharp peak at the discrete stretch sev4 (c=0.6): sev3 31.26, sev4 40.68, sev5 29.82 (x_distortion contrast_weaken_stretch has no intermediate c value). The glass axis is nearly flat: sev3 39.35, sev4 40.68, sev5 39.68 -> gm_ratio=0.1377 overstates blur severity because it embeds the stretch c=0.6 gradient contraction (~0.3 factor). Subtype control: gaussian4 39.24 on pair0 (-1.44 dB vs glass4) confirms the glass advantage is not a saturation artifact, but glass_score=0.3044 stays marginal. All 5 R2 candidates scored below the unchanged winner on pair0; the closest alternative (glass5) also lost on the weakest pair1 (37.15 vs 38.27). Residual zero_crossing_density (target ZC above every simulation by 41-51% relative while all other CI metrics pass) is consistent with blur_glass's unseeded np.random.randint shuffle: the GT shuffle realization is unrecoverable, which explains the content-dependent 38.27-43.57 dB spread and caps simulation PSNR. No candidate met the >40 dB or +2 dB CHANGE rule on any support pair -> NO_CHANGE.
